title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Vectors
content: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks occur when an attacker injects malicious scripts into trusted websites. Types of XSS include: 1) Stored XSS - script is permanently stored in database and executed when requested; 2) Reflected XSS - script is reflected off web server in search results or error message; 3) DOM-based XSS - vulnerability exists in client-side code rather than server-side. Prevention: Context-aware HTML entity encoding, Content Security Policy (CSP) headers (`script-src 'self'`), HTTPOnly flags on authentication cookies, and DOM sanitization libraries like DOMPurify.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Prevention
content: CSRF forces an end user to execute unintended actions on a web application in which they're currently authenticated. CSRF attacks target state-changing requests (like password changes or fund transfers), not data theft. Mitigations: Anti-CSRF Synchronizer Tokens (unique, unpredictable per-session token), SameSite cookie attribute (`SameSite=Strict` or `SameSite=Lax`), and custom request headers (`X-Requested-With`) for API endpoints.

title: SQL Injection Mechanics & Prepared Statements
content: SQL Injection occurs when user input is concatenated directly into a database query string. Common variants: In-band SQLi (Error-based, Union-based), Blind SQLi (Boolean-based, Time-based), and Out-of-band SQLi. Payload example: `' OR '1'='1' -- `. Defense: Prepared statements with parameterized queries (e.g. `SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?`), Object-Relational Mappers (ORM like SQLAlchemy or Prisma), and enforcing least-privilege DB users.

title: JWT Attack Vectors & Implementation Hardening
content: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are widely used for stateless authentication. Common vulnerabilities: 1) Algorithm Confusion (switching RS256 to HS256 using public key as secret); 2) `alg: none` signature bypass; 3) Weak secret keys brute-forceable with hashcat; 4) Missing expiration (`exp`) check. Best practices: Always verify signature with strong secret/key, explicitly white-list expected algorithms (HS256/RS256), enforce short expiration times, and store tokens securely in HttpOnly cookies.
